Marathon Petroleum stock ticked up just 0.28% today, a negligible move after a volatile two weeks that saw the stock climb nearly 10%. The minimal gain today likely reflects a pullback in oil prices as traders bet on diplomatic progress in the Middle East—crude fell on October 20th even as geopolitical tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on Saudi facilities remain the dominant driver of energy markets.

The broader story is that Marathon has been riding a sharp oil rally over the past fortnight. Brent crude spiked above $109 after Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, and that's directly helped refiner margins: the company benefits when crude prices stay elevated while refined product demand holds steady. With US refineries running at 93.5% capacity and oil storage well-supplied at 698.56 million barrels, Marathon is operating in a favorable environment despite today's pause.
